result.title: Seeing at the Edge: Energy Characterization of Vision-Language Model Inference on Edge Platforms
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are moving onto edge devices, but little is known about how much energy they draw on single-board computers with NPU or GPU accelerators, or where that energy goes. We measure total-system energy, latency, and thermal behavior of Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct and its text-only sibling on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-10H NPU and on a Jetson Orin Nano Super, on both CPU and accelerator, and separate the fixed energy of each request from the energy that grows with output length. Because the accelerators use different quantization and serving software, we compare deployment stacks rather than silicon. Three findings stand out. First, NPU offloading makes the Pi a much more efficient VLM platform: it cuts energy per generated token by about two-thirds, leaves the host CPU largely free, and avoids the thermal throttling that the CPU backend reaches in sustained use. Second, an image adds both fixed and per-token energy, but at typical response lengths generating the answer costs far more than processing the image. Third, the Jetson GPU favors short responses through its lower fixed cost per request, whereas the Pi NPU favors longer ones through its lower cost per output token; their energy curves cross near 40 output tokens.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在树莓派 5（Hailo-10H NPU）与 Jetson Orin Nano Super 上测量 Qwen2-VL-2B 及其纯文本版本的整机能耗、延迟与热行为，并把每次请求的固定能耗与随输出长度增长的能耗拆开比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定成本 vs 每 token 成本」的分解及约 40 token 处的能耗交叉点，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的成本权衡与长度泛化提供定量参照，但该文属部署能耗刻画，与 latent 推理机制距离较远，可供核查。
